course_title: Exercise-based rehabilitation, strength and conditioning in musculoskeletal, sports and exercise physiotherapy
course_description:
Exercise-based rehabilitation, strength and conditioning in musculoskeletal, sports and exercise physiotherapy

In PHTY7953 students will advance their knowledge and capabilities in the application of exercise prescription, progression and programming in the management of injury and pathology in musculoskeletal, sports and exercise physiotherapy practice. Students will develop their understanding of exercise-induced adaptations and the use of exercise in the treatment and prevention of musculoskeletal, occupational and sports injuries/conditions and chronic disease. Students will develop skills to design, implement and progress exercise programs at individual and population levels with understanding of pathological and adaptive timeframes and use appropriate outcome measures to guide exercise prescription and progression.

course_aims: To develop students’ knowledge and capabilities in the application of exercise prescription, progression and programming in the management of injury and pathology in musculoskeletal, sports and exercise physiotherapy practice.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand the acute and long‑term physiological adaptations and maladaptations to different types of exercise across the neuromuscular, sensorimotor, cardiorespiratory, and metabolic systems.
Design individualised, safe and progressive evidence‑based exercise programs for diverse populations with musculoskeletal, occupational, sports, and chronic health conditions.
Select appropriate assessment, monitoring, periodisation, workload management and criteria‑driven progression to optimise health outcomes at individual and group levels.
Apply advanced clinical reasoning and behaviour‑change strategies to enhance engagement with exercise programs and support sustainable physical activity participation.
Evaluate and critically reflect on the effectiveness of exercise‑based rehabilitation to improve client outcomes and refine clinical practice.
